extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities and interested public (financial institutions, retailers, lessors, motor vehicle dealers, prepaid/gift card issuers), and members of the public invited to submit PRA comments
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notice seeking public comment and OMB approval to extend Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) clearances for Regulations B, E, M, and Z; describes who is affected, how to comment, statutory/regulatory background, and estimated burden/cost metrics for each regulation. Useful for regulated entities preparing comments or estimating compliance burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be filed by December 23, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the closing date for public submissions for this PRA notice; late submissions will not satisfy the stated comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file comments / where to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties may file a comment online or on paper by following the instructions in the Request for Comment part of the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section; written comments and recommendations should be sent within 30 days of publication to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the particular information collection by selecting 'Currently under 30-day Review—Open for Public Comments' or use the search function on reginfo.gov. The notice also points readers to the Request for Comment portion of the Supplementary Information for specific filing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record disclosures and identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comment—including your name and your state—will be placed on the public record of this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because comments are public, commenters are solely responsible for ensuring they do not include sensitive personal information (e.g., Social Security numbers, dates of birth, driver’s license or passport numbers, financial account numbers, medical records) or trade secrets/commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential as provided by section 6(f) of the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 46(f)) and FTC Rule 4.10(a)(2) (16 CFR 4.10(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may redact or withhold submissions; availability may be delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments placed on Regulations.gov or other platforms can be redacted/withheld under agency rules; availability on public docket may be delayed while agency processes submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA review authority and implementing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PRA requirements, OMB's Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) reviews Federal information collections pursuant to 5 CFR part 1320 and 44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explains that OMB/OIRA approval is required for information collections and provides the web link to reginfo.gov as the portal for PRA submissions and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of review for these collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of Review: Extension without change of currently approved collection, except for new Regulation B requirements, which derive from statutory amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most of the existing clearances are being extended without change; however, Regulation B includes new requirements tied to statutory amendments (CFPB small business lending provisions) and those are reflected in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected public
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected Public: Private Sector: Businesses and other for-profit entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the primary respondents and entities whose paperwork burden is being estimated (e.g., financial institutions, retailers, lessors, dealers, gift card issuers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official PDF for legal/official format
rubrics_metrics.description: This document has been published in the Federal Register. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FederalRegister.gov shows an XML rendition that is unofficial; users should verify against the official SGML/PDF on govinfo.gov for legal research and the official version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation B substantive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation B implements the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA), prohibiting discrimination in the extension of credit and establishing disclosure requirements to assist customers in understanding their rights and recordkeeping requirements to assist agencies in enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation B applies to retailers, mortgage lenders, mortgage brokers, finance companies, and others. CFPB amendments (2023) created subparts A (prior requirements) and B (new small business lending requirements under section 1071). The FTC included estimates for CFPB's new requirements and retained burden estimates for motor vehicle dealers and state-chartered credit unions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation B estimated PRA burden and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated Annual Burden Hours for Regulation B: 3,877,492 hours (Total); Recordkeeping: 1,296,378 hours; Disclosures and Reporting: 2,581,114 hours. Estimated Annual Labor Costs: $159,000,057 (Total); Recordkeeping: $32,783,491; Disclosures and Reporting: $126,216,566. Estimated Annual Non-Labor Costs: A range up to $6 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The non-labor cost range reflects diversity among covered entities and circumstances; the high end may be overinclusive as explained in the supporting statement. These figures are the FTC's PRA burden estimates for Reg B (including FTC-retained populations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation E substantive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation E implements the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (EFTA), requiring covered entities to provide consumers with accurate disclosure of the costs, terms, and rights relating to electronic fund transfers (EFTs) and certain other services; it also establishes recordkeeping requirements to assist enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation E applies to financial institutions, retailers, gift card issuers and others that provide gift cards, service providers, various federal and state agencies offering EFTs, prepaid account entities, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation E estimated PRA burden and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated Annual Burden Hours for Regulation E: Total 7,435,956 hours; Recordkeeping: 251,053 hours; Disclosures: 7,184,903 hours. Estimated Annual Labor Costs: $363,192,555 (Total); Recordkeeping: $6,150,791; Disclosures: $357,041,764. Estimated Annual Non-Labor Costs: $0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the FTC's estimated annual burdens and costs attributed to Regulation E information collection requirements for the covered entities over which the FTC has PRA responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation M substantive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation M implements the Consumer Leasing Act (CLA), requiring covered entities to provide consumers with accurate disclosure of the costs and terms of leases and establishing recordkeeping requirements to assist agencies with enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation M applies to vehicle lessors (auto dealers, independent leasing companies, manufacturers' captive finance companies), computer lessors, furniture lessors, e-commerce lessors, lease advertisers, and others to enable consumers to comparison shop and understand lease terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation M estimated PRA burden and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated Annual Burden Hours for Regulation M: 101,953 hours (Total); Recordkeeping: 30,203 hours; Disclosures: 71,750 hours. Estimated Annual Labor Costs: $6,535,193 (Total); Recordkeeping: $1,936,018; Disclosures: $4,599,175. Estimated Annual Non-Labor Costs: $0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC's PRA burden estimates for Regulation M information collections as set forth in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation Z substantive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation Z implements the Truth in Lending Act (TILA) to foster comparison credit shopping and informed credit decisions by requiring creditors and others to provide accurate disclosures regarding the costs and terms of credit to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation Z pertains to open-end and closed-end credit and applies to mortgage companies, finance companies, auto dealerships, private education loan companies, merchants who extend credit, credit advertisers, acquirers of mortgages, and others. Additional mortgage-area requirements include high-cost mortgages, higher-priced mortgage loans, ability-to-pay rules, mortgage servicing, loan originator rules, and certain integrated mortgage disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation Z estimated PRA burden and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated Annual Burden Hours for Regulation Z: 8,416,441 (Total); Recordkeeping: 561,866 hours; Disclosures: 7,854,575 hours. Estimated Annual Labor Costs: $397,863,549 (Total); Recordkeeping: $13,765,727; Disclosures: $384,097,822. Estimated Annual Non-Labor Costs: $0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC's PRA burden and cost estimates for Regulation Z information collections; some short disclosures (e.g., appraisal disclosure for higher-priced mortgage loans) are provided by the CFPB and are not considered 'collections of information' for PRA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation/division of PRA burden between FTC and CFPB
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of shared enforcement jurisdiction after the Dodd-Frank Act, the FTC and the CFPB have divided the FTC's previously-cleared PRA burden estimates between them; the FTC has assumed all burden estimates associated with motor vehicle dealers and state-chartered credit unions and has added estimates for the CFPB's new Regulation B requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The division reflects enforcement jurisdiction and practical considerations; CFPB's PRA clearance requests also reflect the burden they assume. The FTC's figures include PRA burden for all state-chartered credit unions in many instances to avoid undercounting due to overlapping authority and data limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTC retains PRA burden for certain motor vehicle dealers
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Dodd‑Frank Act, the FTC generally has sole authority to enforce Regulations B, E, M, and Z regarding certain motor vehicle dealers 'predominantly engaged in the sale and servicing of motor vehicles, the leasing and servicing of motor vehicles, or both' (and that assign contracts to unaffiliated third parties); the FTC retains the entire PRA burden for motor vehicle dealers in its estimates below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explains why PRA burden for motor vehicle dealers is retained by the FTC (jurisdictional allocation and practical estimation difficulties) and that this attribution does not change actual enforcement authority.
